question: The Vimana in the Dravidian style of temple architecture is usually in which shape?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pyramidal**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The main temple tower's form a geometrically rising **stepping pyramid (unlike the Nagara style Shikhara that is curving)**.
 
• It represents **Vishnu's most potent weapon, the sudarshana chakra.**
 
• The **Konark Sun Temple's** vimana was** the tallest of all vimanas** before it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7560bb9d85c968dd001543aae8fa0f15285c39d2e30042a21d211b1ed15963fe.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The following are the characteristics of the** Dravidian Style of Architecture**:
 
• The** entry doorway in the centre **of the front wall is known as a** gopuram.**
 
• **Vimana:** The main temple tower's form. It is a geometrically rising stepping pyramid (unlike the Nagara style Shikhara that is curving).
 
• The name for the **crowning piece at the top** of the temple in the** Dravida style is shikhara (**which is shaped like a stupika or octagonal cupola).
